# Phase 1: Math foundations

*weeks 3–4, then on call* · [Track on the site](https://arubad.github.io/AI_Research_Journey/#p1)

At least one company will run a dedicated math interview, from logic puzzles to pen-and-paper derivations. Everything here is HAND: derive on paper, then confirm numerically in a 10-line script. Each derivation is paired with the paper in Phase 3 that uses it, so the math is never studied in isolation.

| # | Area | Derive by hand | Confirm in code (HAND, under 20 lines) | Used in paper | File |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | Probability | Bernoulli → Binomial → Gaussian limit; 68-95-99.7; CLT; multivariate Gaussian | Sample 10k Bernoullis, plot the binomial mean converging to a Gaussian | #9 DDPM (Gaussian forward process) | `derivations/M1-bernoulli-binomial-gaussian-limit-68.md` |
| M2 | Probability | MLE: show minimizing cross-entropy is maximizing log-likelihood | Train logistic regression with both losses, assert identical gradients | #4 Transformer (LM loss) | `derivations/M2-mle-show-minimizing-cross-entropy-is.md` |
| M3 | Probability | MAP: show L2 regularization equals a Gaussian prior | Compare `weight_decay` vs explicit log-prior term | #2 Adam (L2 vs AdamW) | `derivations/M3-map-show-l2-regularization-equals-a.md` |
| M4 | Information theory | Entropy; derive perplexity = exp(H); cross-entropy vs KL | Compute PPL of a tiny LM two ways | #12 Chinchilla (loss curves) | `derivations/M4-entropy-derive-perplexity-exp-h-cros.md` |
| M5 | Information theory | KL(P ‖ Q) vs KL(Q ‖ P): mode-seeking vs mass-covering; which direction the RLHF penalty uses and why | Fit a 1-Gaussian to a 2-Gaussian mixture under each direction, plot | #11 InstructGPT, #13 DPO | `derivations/M5-kl-p-q-vs-kl-q-p-mode-seeking-vs-mas.md` |
| M6 | Linear algebra | Matmul FLOPs: (m×k)@(k×n) = 2mnk; derive 6ND for Transformer training | Count FLOPs for a 124M GPT-2 by hand, check with `torch.utils.flop_counter` | #12 Chinchilla, #17 FlashAttention | `derivations/M6-matmul-flops-m-k-k-n-2mnk-derive-6nd.md` |
| M7 | Linear algebra | SVD $A = U \Sigma V^\top$; Eckart–Young: rank-r truncation minimizes Frobenius error | SVD a fine-tuned ΔW, plot singular values, verify most mass is in top-r | #10 LoRA | `derivations/M7-svd-eckart-young-rank-r-truncation-m.md` |
| M8 | Linear algebra | Eigendecomposition of symmetric matrices; matrix norms (L1, L2, Frobenius, nuclear) and what each regularizes | — | #10 LoRA | `derivations/M8-eigendecomposition-of-symmetric-matr.md` |
| M9 | Calculus | Chain rule for a 2-layer MLP; Jacobians for vector→vector maps | NumPy forward+backward for linear → softmax → cross-entropy, no autograd; assert against `torch.autograd` | #1 AlexNet | `derivations/M9-chain-rule-for-a-2-layer-mlp-jacobia.md` |
| M10 | Calculus | Attention gradient: $\partial\,\mathrm{softmax}(QK^\top/\sqrt{d})V / \partial Q$ | Confirm the √d_k variance argument numerically | #4 Transformer | `derivations/M10-attention-gradient.md` |
| M11 | Optimization | Adam update rule; why m̂ and v̂ need bias correction at step 1 | Your 25-line Adam from Module 1, with and without correction | #2 Adam | `derivations/M11-adam-update-rule-why-m-and-v-need-bi.md` |
| M12 | Optimization | Policy gradient: the log-derivative trick, reward-to-go, why a state-only baseline is unbiased | REINFORCE on a 3-armed bandit, with and without baseline, plot variance | #8 PPO, #19 GRPO | `derivations/M12-policy-gradient-the-log-derivative-t.md` |

**Study order.** Read [CS231n backprop notes](https://cs231n.github.io/optimization-2/) first (the NumPy backward pass is asked verbatim). Then Hamish Ivison's [Introduction to Policy Gradient for LMs](https://ivison.id.au/2026/02/09/policy-gradient.html), which derives REINFORCE → baselines → importance weighting → group-relative advantages in LM notation; read it before touching PPO or GRPO. Supplement with Lilian Weng's [Policy Gradient Algorithms](https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2018-04-08-policy-gradient/) and Chip Huyen's [ML Interviews Book](https://huyenchip.com/ml-interviews-book/) to find gaps.

| `derivations/` | One file per row: the pen-and-paper derivation (photo or LaTeX) |
| `checks/` | The under-20-line scripts that confirm each derivation numerically |
